answer: A sybil defense can work like a vine: trust grows only along verified work links. A newcomer may wander into low-value tasks freely, but to reach paid work it needs a sponsor whose stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats, and each sponsor regrows only one invitation per month of clean history, while raven auditors randomly re-check completed jobs. Faking a thousand identities would require a thousand sponsors, a thousand stakes, and months of honest work first, which costs more than the fraud could earn.
